entry.title: A Fully Programmable Secure Web Gateway
entry.content:
Every secure web gateway on the market works the same way: traffic matches a condition. A terminal action fires. Allow, Block, Isolate, Log. This model has been the foundation of network security for nearly 30 years, and it handles the common case well. But it has a ceiling, and customers with complex environments hit that ceiling regularly.

Earlier this year, we shared our vision to build a truly programmable SASE platform. We also outlined how the term programmability has become diluted by the security industry. Most vendors claim programmability because they have public APIs, Terraform providers, webhooks, and alerting. Cloudflare offers all of those things too, but that’s not enough. True programmability means running your own code — arbitrary logic that you wrote for your specific environment — inline in the policy evaluation path, at the moment a security decision is made.

Today, we’re excited to announce Cloudflare is bringing true programmability to Cloudflare Gateway and DLP (Data Loss Prevention) by integrating it with the entirety of our edge computing platform. We are releasing a new type of Gateway action, Forward, and custom validation functions, available to all Zero Trust plans. These capabilities allow you to use a Cloudflare Worker to transform and manipulate traffic, or to bring your own data to policy evaluation.

The trade-off that every security team faces

For as long as firewalls have existed, businesses have faced a binary choice. You can maintain your own security detection engine — your own firewall, your own proxy infrastructure — with high maintenance overhead and low portability, in exchange for maximum customization. Or, you can accept the constraints of a vendor, offloading the considerable maintenance cost, at the expense of flexibility to solve problems specific to your environment.

In six years of building Cloudflare Gateway, we have heard from thousands of customers struggling with this trade-off. A security team migrating access controls for a critical internal application needs to inject HTTP headers based on JSON Web Token (JWT) claims from their identity provider. The data exists in the request context, but Gateway cannot read the JWT and write the header. So the team stands up a pool of NGINX proxies solely to perform this transformation. That infrastructure now must be patched, monitored, and secured... indefinitely.

Another team wants a Slack notification the moment an employee signs up for a new SaaS service. The policy engine can detect the sign-up event, but it can only Allow or Block. So the team builds a Logpush-to-SIEM-to-Slack pipeline with a 5 to 15 minute delay and no guarantee of delivery. And piles on yet another piece of infrastructure.

Dozens of enterprise customers have asked for warning pages that prompt users for justification before allowing access to sensitive destinations. Most then want to customize the ensuing behavior based on additional context about who the user is and the level of access requested. But serving customized, dynamic responses from a policy engine is exceedingly difficult.

We have offered customers many extension points over the years. But along with every other firewall vendor, it is impossible to build features to cover threat vectors as quickly as they can appear. However, we also recognize that the best solutions are those which are infinitely extensible to your environment.

Why only Cloudflare can solve this problem

Cloudflare is not just a firewall, or a secure web gateway, a content delivery network, or an edge service. Cloudflare is a composable compute platform. Cloudflare Workers already allows customers to run complex logic on our network edge from any of our 330+ locations worldwide. Cloudflare Gateway already evaluates and enforces security policy on user traffic at those same locations, on the same machines, in the same data centers.

Only Cloudflare runs both distributed customer compute and a full-featured secure web gateway and firewall in the same globally distributed network. We have the unique opportunity and ability to combine those functions into the industry’s first completely programmable and customizable SASE platform.

Gateway and Workers were built on the same infrastructure from the beginning. When Gateway forwards traffic to a Worker, that dispatch is a local function call. There is no hairpinning. There is no additional latency from crossing a network boundary. This is the first time that customers will have absolute control over how their proxied traffic is processed, without compromise, using code that they can write and execute without maintaining any sort of infrastructure.

Standalone SASE providers without their own compute platform require you to deploy automation in a separate cloud, manually configure webhooks, and accept the round-trip latency and management overhead of stitching together disconnected systems. No other vendor in this space has a programmable edge compute platform co-located with their security gateway. As threats advance at AI-powered speed, this will provide much needed flexibility and agility for security organizations.

Two Gateway entry points: Forward action and Custom Functions

A new Gateway action type called Forward and a new policy resource called a Custom Function are two distinct ways to call a Worker from a Gateway policy. The Forward action is available in public beta today, and Custom Functions will be available before the end of the year.

Forward action: traffic transformation and proxy

You can customize HTTP traffic behavior with a new policy action called Forward that routes the matched HTTP request to a Worker as a proxy. Policies with the Forward action are evaluated for traffic allowed by HTTP policies. The first matching Forward rule will then be applied to your traffic, and the traffic will be sent to its bound Cloudflare Worker. The Worker acts as inline middleware: it receives the full headers and request body. Your logic can then choose to modify either one (or take another asynchronous action of some kind), forward the request to the origin, receive the response, can modify that too, and return the final response to the user.

import { WorkerEntrypoint } from "cloudflare:workers";import type {  GatewayMiddlewareContext,  GatewayMiddlewareNext,} from "@cloudflare/zt-types";
export class GatewayMiddleware extends WorkerEntrypoint {
  async handle(
    request: Request,
    context: GatewayMiddlewareContext,
    next: GatewayMiddlewareNext,
  ): Promise<Response> {
    // Read a value from the Gateway context
    const clientIP = context.srcIp;
// Add headers before the request reaches the originrequest.headers.set("X-Gateway-Client-IP", clientIP);// Forward upstream and get the responseconst response = await next(request);// Modify the response before it reaches the userresponse.headers.set("X-Processed-By", "gateway-middleware");return response;
  }
}

Gateway handles the TCP connections, TLS termination and re-encryption, certificate management, and HTTP version negotiation. The Worker is responsible only for the transformation logic. You get a customizable, proxy-like extension point for your existing security stack, with none of the operational cost of hosting a traditional HTTP proxy.

Your Workers also do not have to transform the request. A rule’s sole purpose can be to proxy a request to a Worker that receives the full context of the matched request asynchronously: send a Slack message, write to R2, log to an external pipeline, call a webhook, update a KV store. The traffic can continue to its destination, unbothered.

Custom functions: inline policy evaluation

A custom function calls out to a Worker inline during Gateway policy evaluation and returns a value. The function is then exposed as a selector in the Gateway policy builder, and the selector is evaluated against its values. The selector is usable in the condition of any network or HTTP Gateway rule, the same way a built-in selector like Source IP or Content Category works today.

The Worker receives context about the request: source IP, destination, user identity, device posture, HTTP headers, and more, depending on the policy phase. The Worker returns a typed value (string, number, or boolean) that Gateway uses in rule conditions. The contract is simple: data in, value out.

Here is a custom function that parses a JWT Authorization header and returns the user’s role:

export class GatewayCustomSelector extends WorkerEntrypoint {
  async compute(ctx: GatewayContext): Promise<string> {
    const authHeader = ctx.request.headers.get("Authorization");
    if (!authHeader) return "anonymous";
const token = authHeader.replace("Bearer ", "");const payload = JSON.parse(atob(token.split(".")[1]));return payload.groups?.[0] ?? "unknown";
  }
}

With this function deployed, an administrator can create an HTTP policy rule: Custom Function “JWT Role” contains “finance_contractor” with an action of Allow. The custom function becomes part of the rule condition, evaluated alongside every other selector.

Custom functions are not limited to HTTP traffic. Because they receive identity, device posture, and connection metadata instead of the full HTTP request, you can use them in the Gateway Network policy rule builder with arbitrary Layer 4 port and protocol traffic as well.

The Worker itself can do anything a Worker can already do — call external APIs, read from KV or D1, or invoke Workers AI. But from Gateway’s perspective, the function is deterministic: data in, value out.

When to use a custom function or a Forward action

Custom functions are designed for quick, bounded, stateless evaluations of data which can return a shaped response. You should think of their use similarly to data that can already be evaluated in Gateway selectors; that is, calculations on data that exist within a set of criteria, e.g. “Ports within this range,” or “URL paths that match this regex pattern.” The power comes from being able to extend your structured evaluations with arbitrary or internal sources of data, for which you’ll see some examples below.

The Forward action requires a little more planning and preparation. It can be used for powerful transformations inline with users’ live requests, and can manipulate them in complex ways both on the egress and return to the origin service. These should be thought of as transformation functions, something that very few enterprise security proxies even conceptualize today. Workers that use the Forward action should be targeted and designed carefully to avoid adverse effects on the end user’s overall experience.

What you can build

Purpose justification and interstitial pages

A Worker intercepts a request to a sensitive destination and returns an interstitial page requiring the end user to provide a written justification for access. The Worker calls Cloudflare KV to write a session with a TTL, so the user is only prompted once per configured period. It writes the user’s identity and their stated justification to Cloudflare D1, creating an audit trail. Or, you can use Hyperdrive to write that record to any internal database you already operate.

This has been one of our most-requested features for over four years. With a Worker able to process and manipulate HTTP traffic, it’s easy to build to your own standards.

Dynamic HTTP header injection

A custom function parses a JWT from the request’s Authorization header, extracts the user’s role or group membership, and returns it as a selector value. A Gateway rule matches on that value and sets an X-App-Role header on the upstream request. No NGINX proxy pool. No additional infrastructure to maintain.

File inspection and logging

When a file download matches certain criteria, a Worker can send the file to a third-party sandboxing service for detonation and analysis. Or it can write the file in its entirety to Cloudflare R2 as a permanent record for later inspection, without the file ever leaving the Cloudflare network.

Real-time alerting on policy match

A Worker bound to a Forward policy receives traffic whenever a data loss prevention (DLP) profile matches. The Worker sends a message to a Slack channel or PagerDuty endpoint with the user’s email, the rule that fired, and the destination URL.

export default {
  async invoke(ctx: GatewayContext, env: Env): Promise<void> {
    await fetch(env.SLACK_WEBHOOK_URL, {
      method: "POST",
      body: JSON.stringify({
        text: DLP alert: ${ctx.identity.email} triggered "${ctx.rule.name}" accessing ${ctx.request.url}
      })
    });
  }
}

Complex evaluation logic

Traditional expression builders for firewalls are not designed for the kind of computation some organizations need at evaluation time. If you maintain internal risk scoring systems that perform behavioral analysis across multiple data sources, or if you have complex maps of users, groups, and conditional memberships where multiple criteria must be independently true, you can use a custom function as the computational extension that evaluates all of that logic and returns a single value to Gateway.

Performance and reliability

Because Gateway and Workers services run on the same machines in the Cloudflare network, dispatching to a Worker does not introduce a network hop. The performance impact is limited to the execution time of your Worker code itself.

When a custom function fails — throws an exception, times out, or returns an unexpected value — you configure the fallback behavior per function. Default values are required in the custom function contract, so that it’s easy to determine behavior.

Availability and pricing

The Forward action and its integration with Workers are available in a public beta starting today, with Custom Functions expected to be available before the end of the year. At general availability, both will be available for all customers on all plan types.

Traffic dispatched to your Workers is billed as standard Worker requests. The feature works with Workers Free, Workers Paid, and Workers for Enterprise with no restrictions on functionality. Workers Free does have execution time limits and daily request limits, which is worth considering as you scale the volume of Gateway traffic you send to your Workers.

DLP custom functions for inline detection validation

A fully programmable SASE platform extends beyond just Gateway. Our DLP offering — already integrated across Gateway, AI Gateway, Email Security, and more — now supports custom outcomes through integrations with our Compute platform, as well.

Most data security products operate by looking for data that matches known patterns. Customers can typically define regular expressions, word lists, or similar to operate these detections. They can also improve confidence in matching through the use of keywords or context analysis on the request body. But these methods have a core flaw: these types of detections can only tell you when something matches the pattern of data relevant to your organization, not whether this specific instance of data is indicative of data exfiltration or misuse.

As attackers become increasingly advanced, and agents can be used to ruthlessly exploit systems, improving our ability to accurately detect patterns is not enough. To improve accuracy for the data that matters, you need to know whether the data in question is actively relevant to your organization.

To solve this problem, most solutions leverage exact data match, but this comes with its own trade-offs. Customers must prepare, maintain, and transfer reference datasets, then decide how comfortable they are allowing a vendor to manage data from their most sensitive systems. 

Custom validation functions for DLP bridges that gap, and they’re available starting today. These custom functions allow customers to define their own validation logic, using their own source of truth, directly inside a Cloudflare Worker… and apply it everywhere they use DLP to protect their sensitive data.

Credential and secret verification

When a DLP detection entry is matched, an outbound Worker can be dispatched to run validation logic prior to a policy enforcement decision. If you have profiles to detect the use of GitHub secrets, but only care about active secrets, you can use a Worker to first look up the status of a detected key, return a response from the appropriate GitHub endpoint, and then decide whether or not the DLP profile should match the traffic.

import {
  DlpValidation,
  type DlpValidationInput,
  type DlpValidationResult,
} from "@cloudflare/zt-types";
export class DlpValidationEntrypoint extends DlpValidation {
  async validate({ excerpt, start, end }: DlpValidationInput): Promise<DlpValidationResult> {
    const bytes = Uint8Array.from(atob(excerpt), (c) => c.charCodeAt(0));
    const token = new TextDecoder().decode(bytes.slice(start, end));
const res = await fetch("https://api.GitHub.com/user", {  headers: {    Authorization: `Bearer ${token}`,    "User-Agent": "dlp-GitHub-validator",    Accept: "application/vnd.GitHub+json",  },});if (res.ok) return { score: 1.0 }; // token is valid and activeif (res.status === 401) return { score: "veto" }; // token is invalid, discardreturn { score: 0 };
  }
}

What’s next

This is just the beginning of the fully programmable SASE platform. We are actively working on increasing the entry points from which you can dispatch custom functionality to the entire Cloudflare One suite, with Email Security coming next. That doesn’t mean we’re done building: this new architecture will make it easier for us to build first-party features into all Cloudflare One services faster, more flexibly, and with improved developer experience.

It’s also getting easier every day to protect your Workers, agents, and their traffic using Cloudflare One. If you are an Enterprise customer who would like a strategy session for implementation, a preview of the coming functionality, or to be notified about the custom functions beta, please reach out to your account team.

Your organizational security can now do anything a Cloudflare Worker can do. We can’t wait to see what you build.

  • Review the Gateway and Workers integration documentation
  • See example Worker scripts for use in Gateway
  • Teach your agent to build with Gateway and Workers
  • Learn more about Custom functions for DLP

A fully programmable secure web gatewayhttps://blog.cloudflare.com/programmable-gateway-dlp/

entry.title: 电费 9 毛/天：我让一台 9 年前的旧 MacBook 替我上班，它比入门云服务器还能打
entry.content:
副业掘金系列第 1 篇。不辞职、不融资、不买服务器——我用一台 2017 款的旧笔记本跑起了一个真实收费的 SaaS。这篇文章里有：13 倍的性能翻盘实测、四条隧道三条坑的血泪史、一次亲手拆掉自己公网入口的合规决策、以及一个 kill -9 杀不死的进程。全部数据真实可复现。

一、凌晨一点，我做了个被朋友嘲笑的决定

朋友的原话是："2026 年了，你用 9 年前的笔记本当生产服务器？"

我的回答是一张电费账单：

方案月成本备注
轻量云服务器（2C4G）¥50+还要备案、迁移、续费焦虑
Serverless¥20-80流量一上来账单失控
我家抽屉里的 2017 款 MacBook Pro¥27（电费）i7-7700HQ / 16G，60W × 24h × 0.6 元/度

算下来每天 9 毛钱。 一杯奶茶的三分之一，买一台"从不请假的服务器"。

有人会说笔记本不稳定。先别急着反驳，看到第三节——我用数据说话。## 二、产品就 60 行代码，但它解决真问题

做什么？短链 + 点击统计 API。别看不起眼，做投放、做社群、做私域的人天天在用，市面上的同类服务定价 29 元/月起。

技术选型只有一条原则：零第三方依赖。Node 24 内置了 node:sqlite，整个后端一个文件：

const { DatabaseSync } = require('node:sqlite');const db = new DatabaseSync('./data/musklink.db');
// 产品的核心动作：跳转 + 记点击
const link = db.prepare(‘SELECT * FROM links WHERE code = ?’).get(code);
if (link) {
  db.prepare(‘UPDATE links SET clicks = clicks + 1 WHERE code = ?’).run(link.code);  db.prepare(‘INSERT INTO clicks (code, ua, referrer) VALUES (?, ?, ?)’).run(code, ua, referer);
  res.writeHead(302, { Location: link.long_url });
  return res.end();
}

零依赖不是极简主义洁癖，是商业决策：

  • 没有 node_modules，就没有供应链投毒风险
  • 部署 = 拷一个 .js 文件
  • 客户付费点在"点击统计报表"：来源渠道（referrer）、UA、按日聚合——这些我全做了

接入极简，一个 curl 就能用：

curl -X POST http://your-host:3456/api/shorten \  -H "X-API-Key: mk_xxx" \  -d '{"url":"https://example.com/promo","code":"musk","ttl_days":7}'# => { "short": "http://your-host:3456/musk", "expires_at": "..." }

支持自定义码、有效期、免费版 100 条/付费版 10 万条（超额返回 402 Payment Required——没错，HTTP 状态码自带付费墙）。

三、压测翻车 10 倍：性能优化最贵的不是代码，是没测量就动手

服务写完，我先做了基线压测（2000 请求 / 50 并发）。结果当场打脸：

[基线] /health（纯 CPU）    →  2849 req/s[基线] /TxZy（跳转+写库）   →   290 req/s ｜ 平均 165ms ｜ p99 341ms

同一个进程，读写库路径比纯 CPU 慢了 10 倍。 我的第一反应不是改代码，而是把怀疑范围缩小：不是 Node 不行，不是这台 2017 款的 CPU 不行，问题只能在磁盘写。

真相：SQLite 默认日志模式下，每次写事务都强制 fsync 刷盘。290 QPS 不是我的代码在等 CPU，是在等磁盘转圈。修复只用了两行：

db.exec('PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL; PRAGMA synchronous = NORMAL;');// 顺便：所有 SQL 启动时预编译，请求路径零解析开销

复测：

[优化后] 跳转+写库  →  3899 req/s ｜ 平均 11.5ms ｜ p99 28ms

13.4 倍。p99 延迟砍掉 92%。 一台 9 年前的笔记本，写库路径直接追平了纯 CPU 路径。

划重点：优化前先测量。靠猜的话，你大概率会去买新服务器——然后带着同样的瓶颈搬家。

四、公网血泪史：四条隧道，三条是坑，最后我把成功的那条也拆了

笔记本要对外服务，得有公网入口。我一个下午试了四条路：

方案结果
localhost.run建连成功，但匿名模式不返回分配的 URL（改版了）
serveo.netSSH 能连上，转发确认永远不来cloudflaredbrew 安装直接失败（macOS 13.7 已被降为 Tier 3 支持）
tunnelmole成功，30 秒拿到 https 公网地址

到这里故事本该结束。但第二天我做了一件朋友更不理解的事：把唯一跑通的隧道亲手拆了。

原因是一条红线：我查了隧道落地服务器——在境外。技术上国内直连确实能通，但一个面向国内客户的商业服务，把入口架在未备案的境外隧道上，等于把地基放在别人的地雷上。

我把它卸载、杀进程、做了三层审计（进程层/工具层/代码层），确认整个服务零外网依赖。正式路径很清楚：花生壳/cpolar 这类国内正规穿透起步 → 有付费客户后上国内云 + ICP 备案。

这不是矫情。在国内，合规不是成本，是你第一天就比别人多的护城河。

五、kill -9 杀不死的值班员

24/7 服务最怕两件事：进程挂了没人拉，合盖了在睡觉。两个都是工程问题：第一层保险：launchd 托管。 配置只有十行，KeepAlive + RunAtLoad。我做了个残忍的实验——kill -9 强杀生产进程：

上次退出码：-9（被我强杀）当前 PID：30502 ≠ 被杀的 30452  ← launchd 已经把它救活了

强杀后约 10 秒，服务原地满血复活。重启电脑它也会自己爬起来。

第二层：caffeinate -s 常驻，接电源合盖不休眠。它没有 KPI，但它从不请假。

六、生意经：2.8 个客户回本，之后全是利润

最后算账，这是全文最不像技术、但最重要的一节：

  • 竞品 29 元/月，我定价 9.9——不是价格战，是成本结构碾压：边际成本 ≈ 电费
  • 电费 0.9 元/天 ÷ 9.9 元/月 ≈ 2.8 个客户回本
  • 第 3 个付费客户之后，每一分钱几乎是纯利
  • 一年后用利润买正经服务器，这台 MacBook 光荣退役进博物馆

写在最后

造火箭和赚钱，其实是同一个问题：找到那个物理上成本最低、需求真实存在的点，然后用工程师的方式执行。

性能瓶颈不在硬件，在一句 PRAGMA；护城河不在技术，在合规和诚实；服务器不在机房，在你不肯认输的那股劲里。

你的抽屉里是不是也躺着一台被低估的旧电脑？

评论区聊聊你最想让旧设备跑的第一个项目。点赞过 50，我把完整源码整理开源，并更新一篇《从旧笔记本到备案上线：正规军改造全流程》。

技术标签：Node.js ｜ SQLite ｜ 性能优化 ｜ 独立开发。数据均为本机实测，欢迎复现打脸。

电费 9 毛/天：我让一台 9 年前的旧 MacBook 替我上班，它比入门云服务器还能打https://juejin.cn/post/7696783367954726963

entry.title: Deploy With Void
entry.content:
VoidZero's tools such as Vite, Vitest, Oxc, and Rolldown — bundled in one toolchain as Vite+ — have made frontend development faster, but building full-stack applications requires more than just a tooling stack. These applications need server routes, databases, local development environments, and a fast and easy way to deploy ideas to production.

We’re excited to open-source three new products that bring server routing, typed data access, and Cloudflare deployment into a unified Vite workflow.

  • Void Platform: A shared deployment platform for teams to host Void apps on Cloudflare.
  • Void SDK: A composable JavaScript SDK for building full-stack apps with Vite.
  • Void CLI: A CLI for provisioning resources and deploying Vite apps to Cloudflare.

The CLI deploys apps built with the SDK to the Platform. All three products are open-sourced as a single JavaScript package and Vite plugin that you can install via npm install void. With Void, you can build your server and client together, carry types from your database to the UI, and let Void automatically provision the Cloudflare resources that your app uses.

We originally set out to build a single, private platform for all users to deploy apps to. After VoidZero joined Cloudflare, we adjusted our direction to open-source the platform and allow anyone to install because we saw a growing need: companies want to encourage vibe-coded internal apps, but are concerned about security and do not want to give cloud access to every employee. Void addresses this problem.

Void Platform: a cloud platform for your company

The Void Platform is fully open source and you can fork it and adapt it to your needs by integrating your company's systems, customize deployment workflows, build features for your customers, or make it work on other deployment platforms. Use the platform as it is, contribute improvements upstream, or fork it and build only the features you need. The open source code can be used out of the box or as a starting point.

As an admin of a Void Platform, you control access, set resource limits, inspect deployments and usage through the Void CLI or admin dashboard, and provide guardrails so everyone else can ship serious and vibe coded apps to the same shared platform.

By installing a Void Platform, your team or customers have a shared deployment environment in your Cloudflare account on top of Workers for Platforms. Void Platform enables:

  1. Faster prototyping. Your team can quickly build prototypes, deploy them, and share working apps for feedback, without setting up a separate Cloudflare account or provisioning resources for every project. This reduces the time to ship internal apps from days/weeks to minutes.
  2. Non-technical teams building. This workflow also lets teammates who do not normally write code work with coding agents to build and share their own apps. A designer can create an interactive prototype, or an operations teammate can build an internal dashboard, then deploy it to the same platform. All with the right security measures in place.

To self-host a Void platform, you need:

  • A Cloudflare account with Workers for Platforms and R2 enabled
  • A PostgreSQL database
  • An account with your chosen login provider
  • A domain for your apps

Then install Void as a cloud platform by running a single command:

Once your platform is set up, approved users can connect to it via the Void CLI for deployment.

void connect https://api.orange-company.dev

A user builds their app using the Void SDK, which is what powers Void Platform benefits like authentication, framework detection, resource provisioning, and more. In other words, Void Platform only works because of the accompanying SDK and CLI.

Void SDK: zero-config infrastructure

Void turns a Vite app into a full-stack Cloudflare Workers app. You or your agents can write code and Void will automatically infer resource bindings and provision resources such as databases, queues, or AI bindings during deployment.

To get started, add Void as a Vite plugin:

import { defineConfig } from "vite";import { voidPlugin } from "void";import { voidReact } from "@void/react/plugin";
export default defineConfig({
  plugins: [voidPlugin(), voidReact()],
});

The Void SDK ships with adapters for popular JavaScript UI frameworks such as React and Vue, provides file-based API routing, pre-rendering, caching, islands, and end-to-end type safety from the database to your UI.

All of Void’s features are optional and composable. Void integrates with existing application frameworks such as Vinext, React Router, SvelteKit, Nuxt, TanStack Start, and Astro. You can use those frameworks for routing and rendering, while Void handles resource APIs using Hono, migrations, deployment, and authentication with Better Auth.

Let’s take a look at building a server-rendered page, with types inferred from the database query through to the client:

// pages/blog.server.ts
import { defineHandler, type InferProps } from 'void';
import { db } from 'void/db';
import { posts } from '@schema';
export const loader = defineHandler(async () => ({
  posts: await db.select().from(posts),
}));
export type Props = InferProps<typeof loader>;

// pages/blog.tsx
export default function Blog({ posts }: Props) {
  return (
    <ul>
      {posts.map((post) => <li key={post.id}>{post.title}</li>)}
    </ul>
  );
}

By importing void/db, Void provides a local database to your app during development and makes void deploy provision D1 automatically for you in production. This also works for using AI through Cloudflare’s AI Gateway: just by importing void/ai, everything is set up automatically for you.

// routes/api/decide.ts
import { defineHandler } from 'void';
import { ai } from 'void/ai';
export const POST = defineHandler(async (c) => {
  const { question } = await c.req.json();
  const result = await ai.run('@cf/cloudflare/clef', {
    model: 'clef',
    state: {},
    questions: {
      decision: { type: 'noul', instructions: question },
    },
  });
  const probability = result.answers.decision.noul;
  return c.json({
    answer: probability >= 0.5 ? 'yes' : 'no',
    probability,
  });
});

Void’s React router is built for Async React, using transitions and Suspense to enable responsive navigation across screens. When you pair this router with a modern data framework such as fate and UI libraries such as Astryx, you can coordinate navigation, data fetching and mutations through React’s transitions, as well as actions and optimistic updates across your entire application. Together, these pieces let you build apps that feel synchronous on fast networks, gracefully fall back on slower ones, and keep interactions responsive during expensive rendering updates.

If a user does not need Void Platform’s team management features, they can use their own Cloudflare account. Void SDK also deploys to Cloudflare directly.

Void CLI: one deployment command

The Void CLI is the main interface for Void. The CLI manages the platform and deploys the app. It’s built on top of the new cf CLI and works well with agents.

With the Void CLI, you can ask your agent to debug failing requests, read deployment logs, analyze how your app is performing, or have them take care of the full lifecycle by deploying a finished app for you.  

Once your app is ready to deploy to Cloudflare, you can run:

The first time you run void deploy, the CLI will prompt you to log into your Cloudflare account. Void builds your app using Vite, applies migrations, automatically provisions resources, and deploys to Cloudflare or a Void Platform. It can be used to handle the full lifecycle of your project such as building, deploying, and managing your resources and projects, for example:

Similar to how the CLI, and an agent by extension, can manage the entire lifecycle of a Void app, you can also use the CLI to manage a Void Platform:

  • Manage users, project access, and resources
  • Inspect deployments, logs, and rollbacks
  • Monitor platform health and usage

Connect with us

VoidZero’s mission is to make JavaScript developers more productive than ever before. We brought Vite, Rolldown, Oxlint, Oxfmt, and Vitest together in Vite+ for development, bundling, code quality, and testing. Void extends that stack to full-stack application development, letting you and your agents build, test, and deploy entire applications.

We’ve been using the Void SDK, CLI, and Platform in production at VoidZero for the past several months and we are excited to see what you’ll build with Void. Please share your feedback with us:

  • Discord: Step into the Void community Discord server for real-time discussions
  • GitHub: Star the repo, start discussions, and report issues
  • Deploy an app with Void: Quick Start Guide
  • X / Bluesky: Follow VoidZero for updates on X or on Bluesky

Deploy with Voidhttps://blog.cloudflare.com/deploy-with-void/

entry.title: 赛力斯康波：问界2027年进入欧洲市场并拓展全球
entry.content:
快科技10月15日消息，赛力斯集团董事、副总裁康波在2026巴黎车展现场接受央视财经频道采访时表示，问界计划于2027年秋季正式进入欧洲市场，并逐步拓展全球市场。目前问界正积极推进监管合规认证与本地化运营，欧洲版车型同步推进中。

据悉，问界汽车的WVTA欧盟整车型式认证工作已全面启动。

此次巴黎车展上，问界以“智慧重塑豪华”为主题，携问界M9、M8、M7、M6四款车型以及魔方技术平台亮相。问界M9在50万元以上市场已累计21个月保持销量领先，问界M8在40万元级别市场连续6个月销量第一，问界M7累计交付量已突破40万辆。2026年1月15日，问界第一百万辆整车下线，从品牌成立到百万辆达成仅用时不到三年。

问界进军欧洲并非孤例。2026年以来，中国新能源品牌出海欧洲步伐明显加快。中国品牌在欧洲市场份额第二季度已接近11%，比亚迪、吉利、零跑、奇瑞等品牌增速显著。

entry.title: 商务部部长王文涛会见美国苹果公司执行董事长蒂姆·库克
entry.content:
快科技10月15日消息，据商务部官网公告，今日，商务部部长王文涛会见苹果公司执行董事长蒂姆·库克。双方就中美经贸关系、人工智能发展、苹果公司在华业务等议题进行交流。

王文涛表示，在两国元首构建“基于尊重、公平、对等的中美建设性战略稳定关系”的共识引领下，中美经贸磋商取得积极成果。

中方倡导人工智能发展安全可控、普惠向善、治理合作。希望苹果公司发挥沟通桥梁作用，为推动中美经贸关系持续稳定向好发展贡献力量。

当前，中国坚定不移扩大高水平对外开放，持续优化营商环境，消费市场扩容升级，绿色供应链不断壮大，将为跨国企业在华投资向智能、绿色、创新转型提供更广阔空间。

希望苹果公司继续深耕中国市场，共享中国式现代化发展机遇。

库克表示，苹果公司看好中国发展前景，将进一步扩大在华业务，并愿为推动美中经贸关系稳定健康发展发挥积极作用。

此次会面是库克本次中国之行的收官重要政企沟通环节，也是他9月卸任苹果CEO、转任执行董事长后的首次访华，行程覆盖广州、北京两地，贯穿产业交流、政企会晤、生态合作多个维度。

【本文结束】如需转载请务必注明出处：快科技

责任编辑：建嘉

entry.title: Staying Evergreen: How We Automated Secure Access and Repo Hygiene in a Shared Org
entry.content:
Working with outside collaborators can add more work for a repository owner. You need to confirm who still needs access, change permissions as projects evolve, and archive repositories once they’ve served their purpose.

To keep up, repository owners need to track collaborators, deadlines, and follow-ups for each repository. As a project grows, that manual housekeeping becomes harder to keep up with and easier to defer.

We faced this problem in a shared organization where GitHub employees (“Hubbers”) collaborate with customers and partners on product trials and professional services engagements. Our answer was Evergreen, a GitHub App built with native GitHub features. The workflows below exhibit a pattern you can adapt for your own organization.

Meet Evergreen

Evergreen is a GitHub App that automates organization hygiene through two workflows:

  1. Outside collaborator access reviews. Every quarter, each repo’s outside collaborators are reviewed. Keep who you need, and everyone else is removed.
  2. Stale repository detection and archival. Repos with no human activity past a threshold get flagged, warned, and (if still untouched) archived.

Two design principles shaped everything:

Fail secure. If nobody responds to an access review, we don’t leave access in place and hope for the best. We revoke it. The safe outcome is the default outcome.

Never destroy anything. Evergreen will never delete a repository or its contents. Archived repos are recoverable, and every access change is written into the repo’s tracking issue, so reverting a mistake is as easy as a copy-paste to Copilot.

How it works: One brain, many hands

Under the hood, Evergreen is a small Go webhook server running in a container. But the interesting part is the choreography. Every moving piece is a stock GitHub feature: a GitHub App, scheduled actions, webhooks, issues, custom properties, and plain files in a repo. Nothing exotic to reinvent.

A controller that keeps time

A dedicated controller repo acts as Evergreen’s clock and its memory. Four scheduled GitHub Actions workflows fire repository_dispatch events on a quarterly cadence, and the app wakes up and does the work:

Reviews open two weeks before their cleanup runs, and there’s a hard grace period baked in so a stray manual run can never fast‑forward the guillotine. Each workflow also supports workflow_dispatch, so we can trigger any step by hand as needed.

State you can git blame

Evergreen tracks every repo’s status as a JSON file (one per repository) committed to the controller repo under state/repos/<repo_id>.json. The snapshot of who had access, when the review opened, the deadline, who decided, and what happened all lives there. Here’s a completed review where a Hubber kept Alice’s access and let Bob’s lapse:

{  "repo_id": 123456789,  "full_name": "the-org/acme-trial",  "last_seen_at": "2026-04-13T00:05:00Z",  "access_review": {    "deadline": "2026-04-27T00:00:00Z",    "status": "renewed",    "collaborators_at_open": [      { "login": "alice", "name": "Alice Example", "permission": "admin" },      { "login": "bob", "name": "Bob Example", "permission": "write" }    ],    "renewed_logins": ["alice"],    "decided_by": "carol-hubber",    "decided_at": "2026-04-15T16:42:10Z",    "tracking_issue": { "repo_id": 123456789, "number": 42 }  },  "staleness": {    "last_activity_at": "2026-04-15T16:42:10Z",    "warned_at": null,    "archive_deadline": null,    "status": "active",    "tracking_issue": null  }}

The best part: because state is just files in git, the commit history is the audit trail. Want to know why someone lost access last spring? git log the state file. There’s no separate database or bespoke audit pipeline to track.

Issue‑ops, everywhere it matters

Evergreen does its talking through issues inside each repository. When an access review kicks off, every repo gets a checklist issue:

The interaction model is delightfully simple: check the boxes for who stays, then close the issue. That’s it. When the issue closes, Evergreen listens for the issues.closed webhook event, reads the checkboxes, retains the checked collaborators, and revokes the rest, then posts a receipt comment listing exactly what it kept and what it removed.

Only the right humans can pull the lever

Closing an access review issue is a privileged action, so Evergreen guards it. If someone who isn’t a Hubber closes an issue, the app quietly reopens it and posts a note explaining why. Decisions only count when they come from the people authorized to make them.

Informing the right people

Here’s a subtle problem: we know the people who need to respond to a review are Hubbers, but we didn’t always know which Hubber(s) owned a given repository.

Evergreen resolves the right people to notify through a fallback chain:

  1. If a repo sets an evergreen_repo_owner custom property (a @user or @org/team), use it.
  2. Otherwise, look at recent issue and commit authors and cc the ones who are on the access review team, i.e., the Hubbers actually working in that repo.

The result: the right owners get pinged automatically, without anyone maintaining a spreadsheet of “who owns what.”

Fail secure, and fail closed

When a review deadline passes with no response, cleanup revokes every collaborator in the snapshot. We were careful about a subtle edge case: what if some removals succeed while others hit a transient API error? Marking the review “done” while a removal is still outstanding would be a quiet inconsistency, and we didn’t want that.

So Evergreen fails closed. If any removal fails, the review stays pending and the issue stays open, and the next run retries the stragglers. It only records “revoked” once every removal actually succeeded. And whatever gets removed is written into the issue, so restoring access is a matter of re‑adding the handles it listed.

The user experience: automation that feels considerate

Automated housekeeping has a reputation for being the office smoke alarm: loud, easy to ignore, and usually going off while you’re cooking something perfectly fine. We worked hard to make Evergreen feel like the opposite:

  • It comes to you. The work happens as an issue in your repo.
  • It tags the right people. No “who owns this?” archaeology.
  • It’s crystal clear about the ask. Every issue states what to do, the exact deadline, and precisely what happens if you ignore it.
  • It nudges before it acts. A reminder comment lands before the deadline: no surprise revocations.
  • It has an escape hatch. Org owners (Hubbers) can opt out by setting a custom property (evergreen_exempt_from_access_review or evergreen_exempt_from_archive).

Rolling it out carefully

Automation that manages access and archives repositories deserves a careful rollout, especially into a large, active org (ours has 1,400+ Hubbers, and many more customers and partners). We wanted the very first run to be a complete non‑event. A few practices got us there:

Dry‑run first. Evergreen ships with a DRY_RUN mode that logs every write it would make without touching a single collaborator or repo. We ran it against the real org and read the logs like tea leaves until we trusted the decisions it wanted to make.

Overcommunicate. Before flipping the switch, we broadcast what was coming, when, and what people needed to do, so the first issue anyone saw wasn’t a surprise. We found that when you’re telling a large group the same thing for the seventh time, it’s often when many are still hearing it for the first time.

Watch everything with Splunk. Evergreen emits structured logfmt logs to a dedicated Splunk index. That observability is how we caught edge cases in the wild (empty collaborator lists, unusual permissions, repos with issues disabled) and tightened the logic before they mattered.

Respect the platform’s speed limits. When you open issues and post comments across every repo in a big org, you slam into GitHub’s secondary rate limits for content creation: 80 requests/minute and 500/hour. While this is a thoughtful preventative control to avoid system abuse, it requires a bit of intention when automating IssueOps at large scale.

So Evergreen paces itself by construction. It processes repos in batches, spaces out each content‑creating call by a couple of seconds, and sleeps between batches to let the rolling window clear, and it only counts the repos that actually create content, so a quiet quarter where nothing’s eligible still runs fast. We opted for proactive avoidance over reactive back‑off.

Lessons we’re taking with us

  • Make the safe path the default path. Fail secure, then make responding easy enough that failing secure rarely triggers.
  • Use the primitives you already have. Issues, webhooks, custom properties, and git history did the work of a bespoke UI, a job queue, and an audit database.
  • Meet people where they work. An issue in your repo beats a dashboard you’ll never open.
  • Logs are a revert button. Writing every change into the issue turned “oops” into “paste these three handles into a Copilot session.”
  • Respect the limits. At org scale, rate limits aren’t an edge case: they’re the design constraint.

Keep your org evergreen

Routine hygiene is the kind of work that’s easy to defer and perfect to automate. The trick isn’t heroic cleanup sprints: it’s making the boring, safe thing happen on a schedule, with a friendly face and an undo button.

That’s Evergreen. And because it’s built entirely from native GitHub features, you can stand up the same pattern yourself.

Ready to make repository hygiene routine? Start with one recurring access or archival task, then use GitHub Apps, actions, issues, and custom properties to automate the problem away.

The post Staying Evergreen: How we automated secure access and repo hygiene in a shared org appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

entry.title: Cloudflare and OpenAI: Making AI Discovery Better for Everyone
entry.content:
Optimizing your site for AI is of little use if AI can't find it. The answer to someone's question may already be on your website: the installation guide you spent a week writing, or a first-hand account of using a product, with the details that make the difference for whether they buy it. As more people turn to AI for help, you want those systems to find your work, represent it accurately, and send interested people your way. You also want control over how they access your site.

Cloudflare and OpenAI launched a research pilot in July 2026 with those interests in mind. We wanted to find out whether signals from Cloudflare’s network could help ChatGPT users discover new content more efficiently.

Today, we’re sharing early results. So far, the answer is a resounding yes: the pilot has brought previously unknown pages into OpenAI’s search index, giving ChatGPT more sources to draw on to help people find relevant, timely information. Along the way, we’ve learned more about what makes a page worth discovering and how AI systems use the web.

Finding more of the web

The web is full of specifics. Someone fixing a washing machine needs the manual for their exact model. Someone applying for a passport needs the current requirements and fees. Someone choosing a local restaurant needs its latest menu and opening hours. Finding the right page can be the difference between a wrong answer and one that actually helps. These pages can be valuable even if few other sites link to them.

In the previous version of the web, discoverability was getting to the top of a search result page. It was then up to the human who visited your page to determine the value of the information, book that table, apply for that passport. As people increasingly rely on AI to find information and complete tasks, discoverability matters in new ways. AI systems need to find the right sources, understand what's useful, and connect people with relevant information – whether that's through an answer, a citation, or a visit to the website itself.

Cloudflare's network provides signals that can help OpenAI’s search crawler discover more useful pages across the web to surface to ChatGPT users. OpenAI then independently evaluates and ranks how those pages appear based on how relevant and helpful they are. Together, this creates a feedback loop that can improve both discovery and the quality of information people find.

This joint pilot, which used a participating cohort of ~1% of Cloudflare’s total network, has enabled OpenAI to discover and index hundreds of millions of new web pages, helping people discover more useful content and get more questions answered through ChatGPT. By linking back to relevant sources, ChatGPT Search also gives people a way to explore the original content and discover the websites and publishers behind it.

With GPT-6 and Intelligent UI, OpenAI is also making ChatGPT an even better place to shop, learn, and find answers, with more visual, interactive experiences tailored to what people need. This work complements these advances by helping ChatGPT discover more useful, up-to-date information from across the web.

From discovery to useful answers

Finding a URL is only the start. We need to know whether it leads to a page someone can access, whether that page offers anything distinct, and what it might help someone do.

We’ve learned, for example, how easily automated traffic can make a nonexistent page look interesting. Bots repeatedly ask for files that aren’t there. Some sites redirect almost any address to their homepage. Other addresses lead to copies of the same content. Recognizing these patterns gives us a way to cut wasted work before a crawler fetches the page, and improve efficiency in a way that benefits site owners.

We're also testing signals that identify and flag potentially harmful pages, adding another layer of information to support safer, more reliable discovery. A legitimate site can have a single compromised page, such as a fake login form planted by an attacker. Flagging that one page, rather than the whole domain, keeps people safe without penalizing the site owner. Early results suggest these signals can help identify pages that should be kept out of an index.

Making discovery easier

As more people use AI to discover information, website owners have new opportunities to reach interested audiences. For those who choose to make their content available to AI systems, these improvements make discovery easier and more efficient.

Keeping up by fetching every page more often would be expensive for everyone. For a website owner, a crawler that repeatedly downloads an unchanged page adds load without bringing any benefit.

The signals above are how we avoid that. Filtering keeps crawlers away from pages that don't exist or that redirect elsewhere. Change signals tell them when a page is worth another visit, and when it isn't.

There's a balance to get right. Finding new pages can initially increase crawling as those pages are evaluated and indexed. The goal is to keep discovering and stay current while reducing the work that takes. For Cloudflare customers, that means less unnecessary load. For OpenAI, it means more of its search resources are spent on information that helps people.

Making it worthwhile to participate

The next phase will build on what we’ve learned: improve the selection of pages, test faster and more reliable change signals, and measure what happens after content is discovered.

We’re continuing to work with OpenAI to understand how better site discovery can translate into real business outcomes, and we’ll keep sharing what we learn along the way.

Domain owners’ choices matter throughout. A signal about a page doesn’t grant permission to access it. This research uses metadata about the web for search and discovery, rather than sharing page content for model training.

You can use Cloudflare’s AI Crawl Control to understand and manage how AI systems access your website.

Cloudflare and OpenAI: Making AI discovery better for everyonehttps://blog.cloudflare.com/cloudflare-openai-discovery-agentic-web/

entry.title: AutoHotkey V2 零基础快速入门 Part 5 游戏场景明暗阈值采集工具
entry.content:
本工具基于 AutoHotkey v2 开发，用于采集游戏内不同场景的画面亮度数据，自动计算正常画面与黑屏/淡出过场之间的亮度阈值，可用于游戏自动化的场景切换判定。工具支持可视化采样点定位，可直观调整采集位置，输出详细的统计分析与候选阈值。

一、热键功能一览

热键功能说明
F6显示 / 隐藏五个采样点标记
F7重新捕获当前活动窗口，并刷新采样点位置
F8开始 / 停止亮度采集
F9标记当前为「第一场景正常画面」
F10标记当前为「淡出/黑屏过场」
F11标记当前为「第二场景正常画面」
F12查看五个采样点的详细信息（坐标、比例、颜色、亮度）
Esc退出脚本

二、完整脚本代码

#Requires AutoHotkey v2.0#SingleInstance Force; ============================================================; 游戏场景明暗阈值采集工具; ============================================================
; ————————————————————
; 坐标模式
; ————————————————————
CoordMode “Pixel”, “Screen”
CoordMode “ToolTip”, “Screen”
; ============================================================
; 基础配置
; ============================================================
global SampleInterval := 100          ; 采样间隔：毫秒，100=每秒10次
global IsSampling := false            ; 是否正在采集
global CurrentPhase := “UNMARKED”     ; 当前采集阶段
global GameHwnd := 0                  ; 游戏窗口句柄
global SamplePoints := []              ; 实际采样点坐标数组
global LogFile := A_ScriptDir “\brightness_log.csv”  ; 日志文件路径
global PixelMode := “”                 ; PixelGetColor读取模式
; ============================================================
; 采样点比例配置
; ============================================================
global SamplePointConfigs := [
    {Name: “P1”, XRatio: 0.20, YRatio: 0.25, Description: “左上”},
    {Name: “P2”, XRatio: 0.80, YRatio: 0.25, Description: “右上”},
    {Name: “P3”, XRatio: 0.50, YRatio: 0.40, Description: “中央偏上”},
    {Name: “P4”, XRatio: 0.20, YRatio: 0.70, Description: “左下”},
    {Name: “P5”, XRatio: 0.80, YRatio: 0.70, Description: “右下”}
]
; ============================================================
; 采样点预览标记配置
; ============================================================
global MarkerGuis := []           ; 采样点GUI对象数组
global AreMarkersVisible := false  ; 标记是否正在显示
global MarkerSize := 46            ; 标记尺寸（像素）
global MarkerColor := “E53935”     ; 标记颜色
global MarkerTransparency := 220   ; 标记透明度（0-255）
; ============================================================
; 各阶段亮度数据缓存
; ============================================================
global Normal1Values := []    ; 第一场景正常画面
global TransitionValues := [] ; 黑屏、淡出、转场画面
global Normal2Values := []    ; 第二场景正常画面
; ============================================================
; 脚本退出事件
; ============================================================
OnExit CleanUpBeforeExit
; ============================================================
; 启动提示
; ============================================================
MsgBox(
    “游戏明暗阈值采集工具nn”
    . “推荐使用方法：n"</span>     . <span class="hljs-string">"1. 先切换到游戏窗口n”
    . “2. 按 F7 捕获游戏窗口并显示采样点n"</span>     . <span class="hljs-string">"3. 观察 P1～P5 是否位于合适位置n”
    . “4. 按 F6 隐藏或再次显示采样点n"</span>     . <span class="hljs-string">"5. 按 F8 开始正式采集n”
    . “6. 第一场景正常移动时按 F9n"</span>     . <span class="hljs-string">"7. 准备进入场景切换时按 F10n”
    . “8. 第二场景完全显示后按 F11n"</span>     . <span class="hljs-string">"9. 再按 F8 停止并查看结果nn"</span>     . <span class="hljs-string">"正式采样开始时，采样点标记会自动隐藏。n”
    . “游戏不显示鼠标指针也不影响本脚本。”,
    “游戏明暗阈值采集工具”
)
; ============================================================
; 热键定义
; ============================================================
F6:: ToggleSamplePointMarkers()
F7:: RefreshSamplePointMarkers()
F8:: {
    global IsSampling
    if !IsSampling
        StartSampling()
    else
        StopSampling()
}
F9:: SetPhase(“NORMAL_1”)
F10:: SetPhase(“TRANSITION”)
F11:: SetPhase(“NORMAL_2”)
F12:: ShowCurrentSample()
Esc:: ExitApp()
; ============================================================
; 开始采集
; ============================================================
StartSampling() {
    global IsSampling, CurrentPhase, GameHwnd, LogFile
    global Normal1Values, TransitionValues, Normal2Values, SampleInterval
HideSamplePointMarkers() ; 正式采样前隐藏标记，避免污染结果; 窗口不存在则捕获当前活动窗口<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> !GameHwnd || !WinExist(<span class="hljs-string">"ahk_id "</span> GameHwnd) {    GameHwnd := WinExist(<span class="hljs-string">"A"</span>)}<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> !GameHwnd {    MsgBox <span class="hljs-string">"没有找到当前活动窗口。"</span>    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span>}; 清空历史数据Normal1Values := []TransitionValues := []Normal2Values := []<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> !BuildSamplePoints()    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span>; 重建日志文件<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> FileExist(LogFile) {    try FileDelete LogFile    catch as ErrorObject {        MsgBox(            <span class="hljs-string">"无法删除旧日志文件。`n`n"</span>            . <span class="hljs-string">"日志文件可能正在被Excel或其他程序打开。`n`n"</span>            . <span class="hljs-string">"文件位置：`n"</span>            . LogFile            . <span class="hljs-string">"`n`n错误信息：`n"</span>            . ErrorObject.Message,            <span class="hljs-string">"无法创建日志"</span>        )        <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span>    }}try {    FileAppend(        <span class="hljs-string">"Time,Phase,"</span>        . <span class="hljs-string">"P1,P2,P3,P4,P5,"</span>        . <span class="hljs-string">"Average,Minimum,Maximum`n"</span>,        LogFile,        <span class="hljs-string">"UTF-8"</span>    )} catch {    MsgBox(<span class="hljs-string">"无法创建日志文件。`n`n文件位置：`n"</span> LogFile, <span class="hljs-string">"无法创建日志"</span>)    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span>}CurrentPhase := <span class="hljs-string">"UNMARKED"</span>IsSampling := <span class="hljs-literal">true</span>SetTimer CollectSample, SampleIntervalToolTip(    <span class="hljs-string">"采集已经开始`n"</span>    . <span class="hljs-string">"采样点标记已经自动隐藏`n`n"</span>    . <span class="hljs-string">"请按 F9 标记第一场景"</span>,    20, 20)
}
; ============================================================
; 停止采集
; ============================================================
StopSampling() {
    global IsSampling
    if !IsSampling
        return
    IsSampling := false
    SetTimer CollectSample, 0
    ToolTip()
    ShowSummary()
}
; ============================================================
; 生成采样点坐标
; ============================================================
BuildSamplePoints() {
    global GameHwnd, SamplePoints, SamplePointConfigs
    if !GameHwnd || !WinExist(“ahk_id “ GameHwnd) {
        MsgBox “游戏窗口不存在，请先切换到游戏并按 F7。”
        return false
    }
    try WinGetClientPos(&WindowX, &WindowY, &WindowW, &WindowH, “ahk_id “ GameHwnd)
    catch as ErrorObject {
        MsgBox(“无法获取游戏窗口客户区。nn错误信息：n"</span> ErrorObject.Message)         <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span> <span class="hljs-literal">false</span>     }     <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> WindowW <= 0 || WindowH <= 0 {         MsgBox(<span class="hljs-string">"游戏窗口尺寸无效。nn宽度："</span> WindowW <span class="hljs-string">"n高度：” WindowH)
        return false
    }
SamplePoints := []<span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> Config <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> SamplePointConfigs {    PointX := Round(WindowX + WindowW * Config.XRatio)    PointY := Round(WindowY + WindowH * Config.YRatio)    SamplePoints.Push({        Name: Config.Name,        X: PointX,        Y: PointY,        XRatio: Config.XRatio,        YRatio: Config.YRatio,        Description: Config.Description    })}<span class="hljs-built_in">return</span> <span class="hljs-literal">true</span>
}
; ============================================================
; 设置采集阶段
; ============================================================
SetPhase(NewPhase) {
    global IsSampling, CurrentPhase
    if !IsSampling {
        ToolTip “请先切换到游戏窗口并按 F8 开始采集”, 20, 20
        SetTimer HideToolTip, -1500
        return
    }
    CurrentPhase := NewPhase
    switch NewPhase {
        case “NORMAL_1”: Description := “第一场景正常画面”
        case “TRANSITION”: Description := “淡出／黑屏过场”
        case “NORMAL_2”: Description := “第二场景正常画面”
        default: Description := NewPhase
    }
    ToolTip(“当前阶段：`n” Description, 20, 20)
}
; ============================================================
; 定时采样执行函数
; ============================================================
CollectSample() {
    global IsSampling, GameHwnd, CurrentPhase, SamplePoints
    global LogFile, PixelMode
    global Normal1Values, TransitionValues, Normal2Values
<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> !IsSampling    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span><span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> !WinExist(<span class="hljs-string">"ahk_id "</span> GameHwnd) {    StopSampling()    MsgBox <span class="hljs-string">"游戏窗口已经关闭或无法找到。"</span>    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span>}BrightnessValues := []<span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> Point <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> SamplePoints {    try {        Color := PixelGetColor(Point.X, Point.Y, PixelMode)        Brightness := ColorToBrightness(Color)        BrightnessValues.Push(Brightness)    } catch {        BrightnessValues.Push(-1)    }}<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> BrightnessValues.Length < 5    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span>; 计算统计值AverageBrightness := ArrayAverage(BrightnessValues)MinimumBrightness := ArrayMinimum(BrightnessValues)MaximumBrightness := ArrayMaximum(BrightnessValues); 按阶段存入数组switch CurrentPhase {    <span class="hljs-keyword">case</span> <span class="hljs-string">"NORMAL_1"</span>: Normal1Values.Push(AverageBrightness)    <span class="hljs-keyword">case</span> <span class="hljs-string">"TRANSITION"</span>: TransitionValues.Push(AverageBrightness)    <span class="hljs-keyword">case</span> <span class="hljs-string">"NORMAL_2"</span>: Normal2Values.Push(AverageBrightness)}; 写入CSV日志CurrentTime := FormatTime(, <span class="hljs-string">"HH:mm:ss."</span>) Format(<span class="hljs-string">"{:03}"</span>, A_MSec)try {    FileAppend(        CurrentTime <span class="hljs-string">","</span>        . CurrentPhase <span class="hljs-string">","</span>        . BrightnessValues[1] <span class="hljs-string">","</span>        . BrightnessValues[2] <span class="hljs-string">","</span>        . BrightnessValues[3] <span class="hljs-string">","</span>        . BrightnessValues[4] <span class="hljs-string">","</span>        . BrightnessValues[5] <span class="hljs-string">","</span>        . AverageBrightness <span class="hljs-string">","</span>        . MinimumBrightness <span class="hljs-string">","</span>        . MaximumBrightness <span class="hljs-string">"`n"</span>,        LogFile,        <span class="hljs-string">"UTF-8"</span>    )} catch {    ; 单次写入失败不终止脚本}; 左上角实时显示ToolTip(    <span class="hljs-string">"阶段："</span> CurrentPhase    . <span class="hljs-string">"`n平均亮度："</span> AverageBrightness    . <span class="hljs-string">"`n最低："</span> MinimumBrightness <span class="hljs-string">"  最高："</span> MaximumBrightness    . <span class="hljs-string">"`n`nF9  第一场景"</span>    . <span class="hljs-string">"`nF10 过场"</span>    . <span class="hljs-string">"`nF11 第二场景"</span>    . <span class="hljs-string">"`nF8  停止"</span>,    20, 20)
}
; ============================================================
; RGB转感知亮度
; ============================================================
ColorToBrightness(Color) {
    Red := (Color >> 16) & 0xFF
    Green := (Color >> 8) & 0xFF
    Blue := Color & 0xFF
    Brightness := Round(
        Red * 0.2126
        + Green * 0.7152
        + Blue * 0.0722,
        2
    )
    return Brightness
}
; ============================================================
; 数组工具：平均值
; ============================================================
ArrayAverage(Values) {
    Total := 0
    ValidCount := 0
    for Value in Values {
        if Value >= 0 {
            Total += Value
            ValidCount += 1
        }
    }
    if ValidCount = 0
        return -1
    return Round(Total / ValidCount, 2)
}
; ============================================================
; 数组工具：最小值
; ============================================================
ArrayMinimum(Values) {
    MinimumValue := “”
    for Value in Values {
        if Value < 0
            continue
        if MinimumValue = “” || Value < MinimumValue
            MinimumValue := Value
    }
    if MinimumValue = “”
        return -1
    return MinimumValue
}
; ============================================================
; 数组工具：最大值
; ============================================================
ArrayMaximum(Values) {
    MaximumValue := “”
    for Value in Values {
        if Value < 0
            continue
        if MaximumValue = “” || Value > MaximumValue
            MaximumValue := Value
    }
    if MaximumValue = “”
        return -1
    return MaximumValue
}
; ============================================================
; 显示/隐藏采样点切换
; ============================================================
ToggleSamplePointMarkers() {
    global AreMarkersVisible
    if AreMarkersVisible
        HideSamplePointMarkers()
    else
        ShowSamplePointMarkers()
}
; ============================================================
; 重新捕获窗口并刷新采样点
; ============================================================
RefreshSamplePointMarkers() {
    global GameHwnd, IsSampling
    if IsSampling {
        ToolTip(“正在正式采样，不能显示位置标记。`n请先按 F8 停止采样。”, 20, 20)
        SetTimer HideToolTip, -2000
        return
    }
    GameHwnd := WinExist(“A”)
    if !GameHwnd {
        MsgBox “没有找到当前活动窗口。”
        return
    }
    if !BuildSamplePoints()
        return
    ShowSamplePointMarkers()
}
; ============================================================
; 显示采样点标记
; ============================================================
ShowSamplePointMarkers() {
    global GameHwnd, SamplePoints, MarkerGuis, AreMarkersVisible
    global IsSampling, MarkerSize, MarkerColor, MarkerTransparency
<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> IsSampling {    ToolTip(<span class="hljs-string">"正在正式采样，位置标记已被禁止显示。"</span>, 20, 20)    SetTimer HideToolTip, -1500    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span>}<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> !GameHwnd || !WinExist(<span class="hljs-string">"ahk_id "</span> GameHwnd)    GameHwnd := WinExist(<span class="hljs-string">"A"</span>)<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> !GameHwnd {    MsgBox <span class="hljs-string">"没有找到游戏窗口。"</span>    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span>}<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> !BuildSamplePoints()    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span>DestroySamplePointMarkers()<span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> Point <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> SamplePoints {    MarkerGui := Gui(<span class="hljs-string">"+AlwaysOnTop -Caption +ToolWindow +E0x20"</span>)    MarkerGui.BackColor := MarkerColor    MarkerGui.SetFont(<span class="hljs-string">"s10 bold cWhite"</span>, <span class="hljs-string">"Segoe UI"</span>)    MarkerGui.AddText(        <span class="hljs-string">"Center w"</span> MarkerSize <span class="hljs-string">" h"</span> MarkerSize <span class="hljs-string">" +0x200"</span>,        Point.Name    )    MarkerX := Round(Point.X - MarkerSize / 2)    MarkerY := Round(Point.Y - MarkerSize / 2)    MarkerGui.Show(<span class="hljs-string">"NA x"</span> MarkerX <span class="hljs-string">" y"</span> MarkerY <span class="hljs-string">" w"</span> MarkerSize <span class="hljs-string">" h"</span> MarkerSize)    try WinSetTransparent(MarkerTransparency, <span class="hljs-string">"ahk_id "</span> MarkerGui.Hwnd)    MarkerGuis.Push(MarkerGui)}AreMarkersVisible := <span class="hljs-literal">true</span>ToolTip(    <span class="hljs-string">"正在显示采样点预览`n"</span>    . <span class="hljs-string">"红色方块中心就是实际采样坐标`n"</span>    . <span class="hljs-string">"按 F6 隐藏标记`n"</span>    . <span class="hljs-string">"按 F7 重新捕获当前窗口"</span>,    20, 20)SetTimer HideToolTip, -3000
}
; ============================================================
; 隐藏采样点标记
; ============================================================
HideSamplePointMarkers() {
    global MarkerGuis, AreMarkersVisible
    for MarkerGui in MarkerGuis {
        try MarkerGui.Hide()
    }
    AreMarkersVisible := false
}
; ============================================================
; 销毁所有采样点标记
; ============================================================
DestroySamplePointMarkers() {
    global MarkerGuis, AreMarkersVisible
    for MarkerGui in MarkerGuis {
        try MarkerGui.Destroy()
    }
    MarkerGuis := []
    AreMarkersVisible := false
}
; ============================================================
; 显示当前采样点详情
; ============================================================
ShowCurrentSample() {
    global SamplePoints, PixelMode, GameHwnd, IsSampling
<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> !GameHwnd || !WinExist(<span class="hljs-string">"ahk_id "</span> GameHwnd) {    MsgBox(<span class="hljs-string">"没有有效的游戏窗口。`n`n请切换到游戏窗口并按 F7。"</span>, <span class="hljs-string">"没有游戏窗口"</span>)    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span>}<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> !IsSampling {    <span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> !BuildSamplePoints()        <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span>}<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> SamplePoints.Length = 0 {    MsgBox <span class="hljs-string">"尚未建立采样点，请先按 F7。"</span>    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span>}Message := <span class="hljs-string">""</span><span class="hljs-keyword">for</span> Point <span class="hljs-keyword">in</span> SamplePoints {    try {        Color := PixelGetColor(Point.X, Point.Y, PixelMode)        Brightness := ColorToBrightness(Color)        Message .= (            Point.Name <span class="hljs-string">"："</span> Point.Description <span class="hljs-string">"`n"</span>            . <span class="hljs-string">"屏幕坐标：("</span> Point.X <span class="hljs-string">", "</span> Point.Y <span class="hljs-string">")`n"</span>            . <span class="hljs-string">"相对位置："</span> Round(Point.XRatio * 100, 1) <span class="hljs-string">"%，"</span> Round(Point.YRatio * 100, 1) <span class="hljs-string">"%`n"</span>            . <span class="hljs-string">"颜色：0x"</span> Format(<span class="hljs-string">"{:06X}"</span>, Color) <span class="hljs-string">"`n"</span>            . <span class="hljs-string">"亮度："</span> Brightness <span class="hljs-string">"`n`n"</span>        )    } catch as ErrorObject {        Message .= Point.Name <span class="hljs-string">" 读取失败`n错误："</span> ErrorObject.Message <span class="hljs-string">"`n`n"</span>    }}MsgBox(Message, <span class="hljs-string">"当前采样点详细信息"</span>)
}
; ============================================================
; 显示最终采集结果与阈值分析
; ============================================================
ShowSummary() {
    global Normal1Values, TransitionValues, Normal2Values, LogFile
    Normal1Text := GetRangeText(Normal1Values)
    TransitionText := GetRangeText(TransitionValues)
    Normal2Text := GetRangeText(Normal2Values)
    CandidateThresholdText := CalculateCandidateThreshold()
    MsgBox(
        “采集完成。nn”
        . “第一场景范围：n"</span> Normal1Text         . <span class="hljs-string">"nn黑屏过场范围：n” TransitionText
        . “nn第二场景范围：n"</span> Normal2Text         . <span class="hljs-string">"nn阈值分析：n” CandidateThresholdText
        . “nn日志文件：`n” LogFile,
        “采集结果”
    )
}
; ============================================================
; 生成阶段范围描述文本
; ============================================================
GetRangeText(Values) {
    if Values.Length = 0
        return “没有数据”
    MinimumValue := ArrayMinimum(Values)
    MaximumValue := ArrayMaximum(Values)
    AverageValue := ArrayAverage(Values)
    return (
        “样本数：” Values.Length
        . “n最低："</span> MinimumValue         . <span class="hljs-string">"n最高：” MaximumValue
        . “`n平均：” AverageValue
    )
}
; ============================================================
; 计算候选阈值
; ============================================================
CalculateCandidateThreshold() {
    global Normal1Values, TransitionValues, Normal2Values
<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> TransitionValues.Length = 0 {    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span> <span class="hljs-string">"没有记录黑屏过场数据，无法计算。`n请在淡出或黑屏期间按 F10。"</span>}<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> Normal1Values.Length = 0 || Normal2Values.Length = 0 {    <span class="hljs-built_in">return</span> <span class="hljs-string">"两个正常场景的数据不完整，无法计算。`n请分别在两个正常场景中按 F9 和 F11。"</span>}Normal1Minimum := ArrayMinimum(Normal1Values)Normal2Minimum := ArrayMinimum(Normal2Values)NormalMinimum := Min(Normal1Minimum, Normal2Minimum)TransitionMaximum := ArrayMaximum(TransitionValues); 可分离区间<span class="hljs-keyword">if</span> TransitionMaximum < NormalMinimum {    CandidateThreshold := Round((TransitionMaximum + NormalMinimum) / <span class="hljs-number">2</span>, <span class="hljs-number">2</span>)    SeparationGap := Round(NormalMinimum - TransitionMaximum, <span class="hljs-number">2</span>)    return (        "数据存在可分离区间。`n"        . "黑屏最高值：" TransitionMaximum        . "`n正常最低值：" NormalMinimum        . "`n分离间距：" SeparationGap        . "`n候选阈值：" CandidateThreshold        . "`n`n平均亮度低于该值时，可初步判定画面偏暗。`n"        . "平均亮度高于该值时，可初步判定画面偏亮。`n`n"        . "正式自动化时仍建议加入：`n"        . "<span class="hljs-number">1</span>. 多个采样点同步变化`n"        . "<span class="hljs-number">2</span>. 连续若干帧低于阈值`n"        . "<span class="hljs-number">3</span>. 画面重新稳定后再判定场景就绪"    )}; 数据重叠OverlapAmount := Round(TransitionMaximum - NormalMinimum, <span class="hljs-number">2</span>)return (    "正常画面和过场数据发生重叠。`n"    . "黑屏最高值：" TransitionMaximum    . "`n正常最低值：" NormalMinimum    . "`n重叠量：" OverlapAmount    . "`n`n暂时不建议只使用一个固定阈值。`n"    . "建议尝试以下改进：`n"    . "<span class="hljs-number">1</span>. 调整采样点位置`n"    . "<span class="hljs-number">2</span>. 避开角色、文字、火焰和固定UI`n"    . "<span class="hljs-number">3</span>. 增加连续帧判断`n"    . "<span class="hljs-number">4</span>. 增加多个点同步变暗判断`n"    . "<span class="hljs-number">5</span>. 分别设置进入暗场和离开暗场阈值")
}
; ============================================================
; 隐藏提示
; ============================================================
HideToolTip() {
    ToolTip()
}
; ============================================================
; 退出前清理
; ============================================================
CleanUpBeforeExit(ExitReason, ExitCode) {
    SetTimer CollectSample, 0
    ToolTip()
    DestroySamplePointMarkers()
}

三、标准使用流程

  1. 运行脚本 双击 .ahk 文件启动，弹出功能说明窗口，确认后关闭即可。

  2. 捕获游戏窗口 切换到目标游戏窗口，按下 F7，屏幕上会显示 P1~P5 五个红色标记方块，方块中心即为实际采样坐标。

  3. 调整采样位置 观察红色标记是否落在目标采集区域：

    • 位置合适：按 F6 可隐藏标记，避免干扰画面
    • 位置不合适：参考下文「采样点调整方法」修改参数后，重新按 F7 刷新

  4. 启动正式采集 按下 F8 启动采集，采样点标记会自动隐藏，避免污染采集结果。左上角会实时显示当前阶段、平均亮度、最低/最高亮度。

  5. 分阶段标记场景

    • 第一场景画面正常稳定时：按 F9
    • 场景切换、淡出/黑屏过程中：按 F10
    • 第二场景完全显示、画面稳定后：按 F11

  6. 停止并查看结果 再次按下 F8 停止采集，自动弹出结果窗口，包含：

    • 三个阶段的亮度范围（样本数、最低、最高、平均）
    • 阈值分析与候选阈值建议
    • CSV 日志文件路径

  7. 查看采样点详情（可选） 按下 F12 可查看每个采样点的屏幕坐标、相对比例、颜色值、亮度值。

四、采样点位置调整方法

工具采用窗口相对比例定位采样点，调整时只需修改脚本顶部的 SamplePointConfigs 配置数组，无需改动核心代码。

参数说明

  • XRatio：水平方向比例，0.00 = 窗口最左侧，1.00 = 窗口最右侧
  • YRatio：垂直方向比例，0.00 = 窗口最顶部，1.00 = 窗口最底部
  • Description：采样点备注，仅用于展示

调整示例

  • 中间点 P3 向下移动：将 YRatio: 0.40 改为 YRatio: 0.55
  • 左上点 P1 向中间靠拢：将 XRatio: 0.20 改为 XRatio: 0.30

修改完成后保存脚本，按 F7 即可刷新标记位置。

五、核心功能说明

1. 亮度计算

采用人眼感知加权亮度公式：

亮度 = 红×0.2126 + 绿×0.7152 + 蓝×0.0722

亮度范围 0~255，更符合真实视觉感受。

2. 阈值判定逻辑

采集完成后自动分析两组数据分布：

  • 可分离区间：黑屏最高亮度 < 正常画面最低亮度

    • 输出候选阈值（取两者中间值）
    • 亮度低于阈值判定为偏暗，高于判定为偏亮
    • 同时给出自动化优化建议

  • 数据重叠：黑屏最高亮度 ≥ 正常画面最低亮度

    • 提示重叠量，不建议使用单一固定阈值
    • 给出优化方向：调整采样点、避开UI/角色、增加连续帧判断、双阈值方案等

3. 数据日志

所有采样数据自动保存为 brightness_log.csv（脚本同目录），包含时间戳、阶段、五个点亮度值、平均/最低/最高亮度，可用于后续二次分析。

4. 防污染设计

正式采集开始时，采样点标记会自动隐藏，避免红色标记被像素读取到，保证采集数据准确。

💡 建议每个阶段保持采集 3~5 秒，足够的样本量会让阈值计算更准确；尽量避开角色、动态UI、火焰等亮度频繁变化的区域。

entry.title: Chirp Pong
entry.content:
Tool: Chirp Pong

Another game experiment - I wanted to see if it was feasible to have a two player game on two separate phones running in static HTML where the networking code uses chirps sent via the microphone. It seems to work!

Build a two player competitive pong like game where two players use their phones close to each other and the game state is sent via audio noises which the web microphone API can interpret - but add graphical and gameplay twists to make it a lot more fun and intertwine than pong

Claude Opus 5.5 Extra in Claude Code.

entry.title: The Next Developer Interface Is Ambient Intelligence
entry.content:
For most of my career, building software started with the same setup: keyboard, mouse, editor, terminal, browser, and an impressive number of tabs I was definitely going to look at later. The tools changed, but the relationship did not. Like most developers, I learned commands, memorized shortcuts, and adapted my thinking to the machine.

AI is changing that relationship and not because I can prompt my way to some workable code. It’s more because the system behind it can understand a repository, choose the right model, plan work, use tools, edit files, run commands, inspect failures, and keep going within boundaries the developer controls.

We’ve made it possible for a developer to describe an outcome, and GitHub Copilot can gather repository context, inspect symbols and dependencies, edit files, run tests, and revise the implementation. In the IDE, agent mode keeps that loop interactive. GitHub Copilot coding agent can take an issue into an isolated GitHub Actions-powered environment and return a pull request for review. This is not just faster coding. It is the shift from issuing commands to making intent executable. The developer still owns the outcome, but the work looks subtly different.

AI-assisted development compresses that chain of events. We spend less time navigating tools and more time setting direction, supplying context, defining constraints, and reviewing evidence. The development workflow now is about understanding the structure of codebases, the customer, and what a good solution should feel like.

This makes developers’ jobs even more important, and their time more valuable. It makes judgment more valuable. It makes taste more valuable. An agent can generate three implementations before you finish your tea, but someone still has to decide whether the abstraction belongs, the migration is safe, the tests prove anything useful, and the result solves the problem.

That is the most important change in the craft: the developer remains accountable for the outcome, even as more mechanics are delegated.

So what does this mean for the emerging developer workflow? The goal is to embed AI into the workflow, not beside it. It’s more of an ambient intelligence.

That requires portable context. MCP connects agents to tools and services; repository instructions and skills encode conventions; hooks enforce policy and validate output. Simpler interfaces need explicit context underneath.

I see three layers: modality captures intent; the harness plans and acts; the control plane lets developers inspect, redirect, and approve. The best products connect all three without surrendering control.

Together, they let developers move across text, voice, and physical controls without losing context.

Why physical controls are interesting again

I, and many others in the maker community, have been experimenting with ambient control devices, from inexpensive hackable picture frames to ESP32 devices with screens attached. Agentic coding is past just a keyboard and a terminal into alternative interfaces.

Getting this kind of technology into everyone’s hands is something that I’m very passionate about and so over the past 18 months we’ve been working with Logitech on their MX Keypad and how it can help this new way of working.

The Logitech MX Keypad turns familiar developer actions into programmable inputs to accelerate workflows that are ambient and contextual to the work devs are doing. In GitHub Copilot app, a key can submit a parameterized prompt, open or resume a Copilot session, invoke an IDE command, or trigger a multi-step sequence. The hardware earns its place only when that shortcut removes enough friction to keep you in the code, but still gives you control.

Physical controls work when an action repeats often enough that removing a few steps preserves concentration. Not every developer needs another device on the desk, and not every interruption deserves a key. However, with this experience the developer decides which actions earn that shortcut and when the keyboard, command palette, or voice is better. Maintaining flow is the key, and a good interface gives some of that attention back.

GUIs made software visual. Mouse made navigation easier. The web made it connected. Mobile made touch natural. Agents add intent and action. The interface now includes ambient control.

The interface moves into the background

That is why GitHub worked with Logitech to integrate the GitHub Copilot app directly into the experience. Developers can run agentic workflows in control, map a repeated prompt, start or resume a session, and decide through real use whether a physical control helps you stay in flow.

This is still early, so the important questions are engineering questions. How much repository and organizational context should an agent retain? Which tool calls can run automatically? How should credentials, network access, and secrets be scoped? What evidence should accompany a change? How do multiple agents coordinate without duplicating work or creating conflicting pull requests? Products such as MX Keypad let us explore one practical part of that system: how developers invoke, steer, and resume agentic work without losing focus.

For decades, developers learned to speak computer: syntax, commands, APIs, shortcuts, and the occasional incantation copied from a seven-year-old issue comment. Now computers are getting better at meeting us halfway. The best interface will not have the most panels or AI buttons. It will understand enough context, preserve meaningful control, and get out of the way so we can build software that matters.

The goal is not to remove developers from the work. It is to remove friction around the work. Pairing MX Keypad with GitHub Copilot Pro+ gives developers a concrete experiment: choose one repeated interruption, map it to a control, and see whether it preserves focus.

If you want to try it, you can do so here and get three months of GitHub Copilot Pro+.

The post The next developer interface is ambient intelligence appeared first on The GitHub Blog.

The next developer interface is ambient intelligencehttps://github.blog/news-insights/company-news/the-next-developer-interface-is-ambient-intelligence/
